- Overestimate prices in the short term after sentiment spikes (especially >0.6) — model tends to overshoot and then correct.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is low or negative (especially <0.3) — model is overly conservative.
- Model consistently overreacts to recent price spikes (e.g., 72+ → forecast 73+ → true often 72.5–73.0).
- Mean reversion bias: model holds onto recent highs longer than true price tends to revert to 70–72 range.
- Forecast horizon 30d: model often lags 1–2 days behind true price movement, especially when sentiment is volatile.
- When sentiment is rising (0.2–0.7), model tends to over-forecast 1–2 days ahead; when sentiment is falling, under-forecast.
- Avoid extrapolating recent trend without sentiment confirmation — sentiment <0.3 often signals a correction, not continuation.
- Model overweights recent 5–7 day history when sentiment is positive — should dampen momentum if sentiment is weak.
